                                                       NOTE

                 Information is based on a survey of excepted positions in the Federal
                 Civil Service as of September 15, 1972. Positions included are those to
                 which appointments are made by the President, positions under Schedule
                 C of the Civil Service Rules, Noncareer Executive Assignment positions in
                 General Schedule grades 16 , 17 , and 18, other excepted positions at
                 GS- 12 (or equivalent) and above and positions under specified Schedule A
                 and B authorities .


                                                      LEGEND
Type of appointment :
   PAS           Presidential appointment, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate.
   PA            Presidential appointment.
   PL            Positions excepted from Civil Service rules and regulations by statutes.
    NEA            Positions at GS-16, 17, and 18 authorized to be filled by Noncareer Executive Assignment
                     under Executive Order 11315 of November 17, 1966.
    A              Positions excepted from Civil Service rules and regulations, not of a confidential or policy
                     determining character for which it is not practical to hold any kind of examination.
    B              Positions excepted from Civil Service rules and regulations, not of a confidential or policy
                     determining character, for which it is not practical to hold a competitive examination.
    C              Positions of a confidential or policy determining character which are excepted from the compet-
                      itive service to which appointments may be made without examination by the Commission.
Incumbent : Applies only when bipartisan membership is required by statute .
    D              Democrat.
    I              Independent.
    R              Republican.
Tenure :
    S              Status in position .
    VP             Veteran's preference.
    VP-S           Veteran's preference with status in position .
    CA             Career Ambassador .
    CM             Career Minister .
    C              Career.
    NC             Noncareer.
    M              Military incumbent.

Grade:
    GS             General Schedule of the Classification Act of 1949 .
    GG             Administrative grades similar to GS grades.
     WG (WB) ,     Blue-collar positions where the pay is established at the local prevailing rate in the community.
      (WS)
    FI (FSIO)      Foreign Service Information Officer.
     FO (FSO)      Foreign Service officer .
    FR (FSRO)      Foreign Service Reserve Officer.
    FSRU           Foreign Service Reserve Unlimited Officer.
    FS (FSS)       Foreign Service staff .
    PES            Postal Executive Schedule :
    AD             Administratively determined.
Other:
    NE             Grade not established .
    p.d.           Per diem-daily rate of pay.
    p.h.           Per hour-hourly rate of pay.
    W.c. (W.o.c.) Without compensation.
    I(W.a.e . )   Intermittent, when actually employed.
     NOTE : If no date is given under "Expires " column, appointment has no statutory limit .                          III

                                APPENDIX No. 1

MEMORANDUM ON FEDERAL POSITIONS EXCEPTED FROM THE COMPETITIVE
                   SYSTEM BY THE CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION
                                                                                            10

Authority
    By Executive order, the President has authorized the Civil Service Com-
mission to exempt from the competitive civil service positions which otherwise
would be subject to the Civil Service rules and regulations governing appoint-
ment and employment, generally. Civil Service Rule VI defines schedules A, B,
and C and grants authority for the Civil Service Commission to list positions
in these excepted schedules. Under Civil Service Rule IX, which established
the Executive Assignment System for positions in grades GS-16, GS-17, and
GS-18, the Commission may except positions and authorize agencies to fill




                                                                                                EI
                                                                                                 /A
them under noncareer executive assignment.
  The Commission has been given the authority to revoke schedule A, B,
and C listings. It also periodically reviews exceptions made under Rule IX
and, after consultation with the agency concerned, revokes exceptions of execu-
tive assignment positions which no longer meet the criteria for exception.                 IA/P
    The Commission makes decisions about exceptions and revocations after
consideration of agency justifications and its own independent reviews and
analyses. These decisions are made by the Commissioners personally and are
not delegated .
Categories of exceptions
     Noncareer executive assignment. These assignments are made to positions
in grades GS-16 , GS-17, and GS-18 which are either of a top policy-determining
character or have a close and confidential working relationship to a top policy
official. The positions are of the type which share with Presidential appointees
the advocacy of current Administration policies and help assure control of the




                                                                                            TY
                                                                                         SI
executive machinery of Government by the political party in power.




                                                                                         b.
     Schedule C.    This schedule is for positions of a confidential or policy-
determining character not in grades GS-16, GS-17, or GS-18.
    Schedule A. This schedule is for positions, not of a confidential or policy-
determining character, for which it is not practicable to hold any kind of
examination, either competitive or noncompetitive. Examples are positions of
attorneys for which examination is forbidden by law, student interns, and
certain part-time jobs depending on residency in isolated locations.
    Schedule B. This schedule is for positions, not of a confidential or policy-                 1
determining character, for which it is not practicable to hold a competitive
examination, but for which a noncompetitive examination (meeting basic
requirements) is required, such as communications intelligence positions in a
military department.
Filling excepted positions
     Agencies generally establish qualification requirements for excepted
                                                                                            RI
positions, although the Civil Service Commission does this for positions listed              /
                                                                                               V
in schedule B and for positions authorized to be filled by noncareer executive
assignment. The Commission must approve the qualifications of all appointees
                                                                                            E
                                                                                            V




to positions in grades GS-16, GS-17, and GS-18 .
                                                                                         RI
                                                                                         /




Removals from excepted positions
    Because of their policy-determining or confidential nature, positions
authorized to be filled by noncareer executive assignment and positions in
schedule C may be subject to change in a change of National Administration.
However, some incumbents of these and other excepted positions are entitled
to certain protections, which are outlined in the table on the following page .

                                                        APPENDIX No. 3-PAY SCHEDULES

                                                   FEDERAL SALARY SCHEDULES 1973

     Initial appointments to positions under the Classification Act are made at the minimum rate of the grade. Authority exists for ap-
pointment athigher rates for persons of unique qualifications or forpersons qualified for positions which the Government finds unusually
difficult to fill, such as scientific, engineering, medical, and research positions. Special salary schedules are established and periodically
revised by the Civil Service Commission for some of these positions, and Commission approval is required before an agency can place
a"uniquely qualified" person at a rate in the excess of minimum rate for grade 13 and above.
     Step increases are granted at the end of 52 weeks for the first 3 steps, at the end of 104 weeks for the next 3 steps, and at
the end of 156 weeks for steps 7, 8, and 9 if the employee performs satisfactory work at an acceptable level of competence. Rates of
pay established at $36,000 and above under the Executive Schedule may be increased pending the results of a study commission to be
established under Public Law 90-206. This would relieve the compression of top salaries under the General Schedule and Foreign Service
Officer Schedule which are now limited to the rate for Level V at $36,000. These schedules may be changed under annual reviews as
provided in subchapter I, Chapter 53, Title 5, U.S.C.
